plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE, sex- and age-adjusted
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a gene-level raw count matrix from Salmon (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples, counts.csv) with a sample table (metadata.csv: sample, condition, sex, age) for 6 treated vs 6 control human adipose samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is which genes differ between treated and control, with the explicit complication that subjects differ in sex and that the two groups are NOT matched on age — so age is a confounder of the treatment contrast, not a nuisance that can be ignored.

The plan therefore has three parts. T1S1 establishes sample structure before any test: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes, and — the step that matters most here — a quantitative check of how sex and age track the condition labels and the leading PCs (age difference between arms, sex x condition table, PC-covariate correlation, variance inflation of the design). If age is severely confounded with condition (e.g. near-complete separation), the treatment coefficient is not identifiable apart from age, and the step must say so before the model is fit rather than after.

T1S2 fits the model that answers the question: DESeq2 negative-binomial GLM on the raw counts with design ~ sex + age_c + condition, where age is mean-centered and sex is a factor, so the condition coefficient is the treatment effect adjusted for sex and age. Covariates go in the design as fixed effects — the counts are never pre-corrected or residualized, which would understate the standard errors. Pre-filter is minimal (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size); normalization is median-of-ratios size factors inside the model; Wald test on the condition coefficient with control as the explicit reference level; apeglm shrinkage for reporting and ranking; BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05. With 6 per group DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts, and those NAs are reported separately from the independent-filter NAs.

T1S3 is a robustness check that the knowledge base treats as the standard second opinion at this replicate count: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test with TMM normalization on the identical filtered matrix and identical design, plus a sensitivity refit without the age term. Two things get reported: the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set, and how far the gene list moves when age is dropped — the direct empirical measure of how much the age imbalance is driving the answer.

T1S4 assembles the report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, gene table carrying both unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE, counts of tested and significant genes, the design formula and contrast written out, and sessionInfo. No enrichment step is planned — the question asks which genes differ, and gene-set analysis was not requested.

Power is the honest limit: 6 vs 6 with two covariates leaves 8 residual degrees of freedom, so the study detects only large, consistent effects, and a null result is weak evidence of no effect. This must be stated, not buried.

steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1-T1S3. Place the fit diagnostics before the gene tables: the MA plot of the condition contrast with significant genes marked, the DESeq2 dispersion plot with per-gene estimates, fitted trend and shrunken values, and the p-value histogram from T1S2 with its shape stated. Then the gene table, ranked by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change and carrying baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue and padj, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Add a volcano plot and a heatmap of VST values for the top genes, annotated by condition, sex and age so a reader can see whether an apparent treatment gene tracks the covariates instead. State in the report header: the design formula ~ sex + age_c + condition, the contrast (condition, treated vs control) with control as reference, the pre-filter rule, alpha = 0.05 with BH and independent filtering, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number significant, the number of NA p-values by cause, the DESeq2/edgeR intersection size, and the result of the age-sensitivity refit. Close with the confounding summary from T1S1 and an explicit power statement: 6 vs 6 with two covariate terms leaves 8 residual degrees of freedom, so only large consistent effects are detectable and a null is weak evidence of no effect. Attach sessionInfo, all package versions, and any random seed used.
steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers the research question. Its job is to make the treatment effect readable and its limits unmissable, given a small cohort whose arms are not age-matched.
acceptance_criteria: MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram appear before the gene tables, each with a one-line statement of what it shows

The gene table is ranked by the shrunken log2 fold change and contains baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue and padj, with apeglm named as the shrinkage estimator
The report header states the design formula, the named contrast with its reference level, the filter rule, alpha, the adjustment method, n genes tested, n significant, and NA counts by cause
Heatmap of top genes is annotated by condition, sex and age
The confounding summary from T1S1, the DESeq2/edgeR intersection size, and the age-sensitivity refit outcome are all reported
sessionInfo, package versions and any seed are attached with the results
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit since shrinkage does not change the test
Report the number of DE genes at padj < 0.05 and state the cutoff explicitly
Do not add gene-set or pathway enrichment — the research question asks which genes differ and enrichment was not requested
State the power limitation and the age-confounding caveat in the report body, not only in a footnote
Do not describe any gene as treatment-responsive on the basis of fold change alone when its padj is not significant
caveats: A gene that is significant in the age-adjusted model but whose expression tracks age within arms deserves explicit flagging rather than a mechanistic story
With 12,000 genes and 12 samples, the top of the list by shrunken effect size is still subject to selection effects; effect sizes reported here are optimistic for the discovery cohort

grounding.reason: R-0087 requires the MA and dispersion plots as fit diagnostics, R-0085 requires both shrunken and unshrunken log2FC with lfcSE and ranking on the shrunken value, R-0041 fixes the reported fields, and R-0086 the reproducibility record.
